question: Which bar chart style places sub-category bars directly on top of each other to show a total?

options.A: Grouped bar chart
options.B: Stacked bar chart
options.C: Simple bar chart
options.D: Scatter plot chart

explanation: A stacked bar chart segments a single bar to show both individual parts and the combined total. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T7#GNS217_U4_T7_h3)

question: Where should a urinary drainage bag always hang relative to the patient's bladder?

options.A: Below the level of the bladder
options.B: Flat on the floor next to the bed
options.C: Above the level of the bladder
options.D: Level with the patient's chest

explanation: Always keep it lower than the bladder! Gravity keeps the urine flowing away from the body and stops nasty germs from creeping back up. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T15#GNS212_U1_T15_h5)

question: What is the correct way to apply prophylactic eye ointment in a newborn?

options.A: Flood the entire closed eyelid with liquid solution
options.B: Massage the upper eyelid vigorously after application
options.C: Apply into the lower conjunctival sac without touching the eye
options.D: Place the ointment directly onto the center of the cornea

explanation: Spot on! Putting it in the lower sac keeps the tube clean and protects the baby's eye from accidental injury. You're thinking like a real nurse! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h6)

question: Why do many teenagers shy away from standard healthcare clinics for reproductive health needs?

options.A: They fear harsh judgment, stigma, and a lack of confidentiality from staff
options.B: They prefer to use complex surgical procedures at home
options.C: They are completely unaware that health facilities exist in their towns
options.D: They are legally forbidden from entering government hospitals

explanation: Spot on. Fear of being scolded or having their privacy broken stops many young people from getting the care they need early on. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T5#GNS216_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the surest way to confirm a diagnosis of vulval cancer?

options.A: Pelvic ultrasound
options.B: Complete blood count
options.C: Urinalysis and culture
options.D: Tissue biopsy

explanation: Correct! Taking a small tissue sample (biopsy) is the only definitive way to confirm if a growth is truly cancerous. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T8#GNS216_U5_T8_h5)

question: What type of dressing is typically applied immediately after a drainage tube is pulled out?

options.A: An airtight sterile dressing
options.B: A wet saline compress wrap
options.C: An open gauze pad without tape
options.D: A rigid plastic protective shell

explanation: An occlusive or airtight sterile dressing is placed over the fresh wound site to seal the opening and protect it from outside bacteria while it closes. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h7)

question: Why do lab staff test new batches of agar plates using known, trusted strains of bacteria?

options.A: To prove that all bacteria can survive without any oxygen
options.B: To confirm the media supports proper microbial growth
options.C: To measure the exact room temperature of the building
options.D: To clean the interior glass walls of the laboratory incubator

explanation: Quality control is key! Testing the plates beforehand makes sure our materials are in top shape before real patient samples arrive. [learn more](GST114_U5_T4#GST114_U5_T4_h7)

question: Why do some joints in our body, like the ones in the skull, not move at all?

options.A: To help pump blood through the skeletal system
options.B: To store extra calcium for the growing skeleton
options.C: To provide protection for underlying organs
options.D: To allow muscles to attach more firmly to bone

explanation: Spot on! Immovable joints act like a solid helmet, keeping delicate organs like your brain safe and sound. [learn more](GNS121_U3_T6#GNS121_U3_T6_h1)

question: What happens to sealed sharps containers after they are filled in the hospital?

options.A: They are washed out with soap and water for reuse in the children's ward
options.B: They are emptied into general waste bins for easy community recycling
options.C: They are encapsulated in concrete or buried in engineered sanitary landfills
options.D: They are dissolved entirely using basic liquid hand sanitizers

explanation: Well done! Sealing them in concrete or deep landfills ensures nobody gets accidentally poked by old needles later. [learn more](GNS122_U5_T3#GNS122_U5_T3_h7)

question: According to Maslow, what must be met first before a person worries about higher career goals?

options.A: Advanced leadership training courses
options.B: Basic survival and safety needs
options.C: Complete clinical independence
options.D: Personal social media recognition

explanation: Just like building a house, you need a solid foundation. Basic needs like food, rest, and safety come first before we focus on big career heights. [learn more](GST321_U3_T7#GST321_U3_T7_h2)

question: A patient takes strong painkillers daily for tummy cramps instead of seeing a doctor. What is the major danger here?

options.A: The abdominal muscles will become permanently paralyzed
options.B: The underlying disease, such as appendicitis, goes undiagnosed until it worsens
options.C: The body will stop producing natural digestive enzymes
options.D: The patient will develop an instant allergy to all known antibiotics

explanation: Well done! Masking the pain with drugs doesn't cure the problem; it just keeps you quiet while a serious condition gets worse. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T4#GNS215_U4_T4_h6)

question: Why is continuous quality improvement important after putting a team care plan in place?

options.A: To punish team members who make minor documentation errors
options.B: To increase the paperwork burden for community nurses
options.C: To identify weaknesses and update processes for better patient results
options.D: To prove to the government that the clinic has extra funding

explanation: Brilliant! Quality improvement is all about learning and growing so we can give our patients better care every single day. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h7)

question: How long does the post-natal period (puerperium) typically last in clinical practice?

options.A: Six months
options.B: Two weeks
options.C: Six weeks
options.D: Three months

explanation: You'll see this time and again in midwifery! The post-natal period is officially defined as the first six weeks after childbirth when the mother's body returns to its pre-pregnant state. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h1)

question: What is the normal pH range for human arterial blood?
explanation: The body loves balance! Normal arterial blood pH is tightly kept between 7.35 and 7.45 so that enzymes and cells can do their jobs properly. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T7#GNS123_U2_T7_h6)

question: Which of the following is a common misconception about modern contraceptives?

options.A: They cause permanent infertility after stopping use
options.B: They require daily surgical procedures to remain active
options.C: They always cure infectious diseases instantly
options.D: They make hair grow faster all over the body

explanation: A widespread myth is that using birth control makes a woman permanently unable to have children later, which nurses must actively correct. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T023#GNS226_U6_T023_h6)

question: Which emotional response is very common in patients who are newly dealing with sensory loss?

options.A: A sudden surge of euphoria and overconfidence
options.B: Aggressive hostility directed exclusively at medical staff
options.C: Grief over lost independence and feelings of isolation
options.D: Complete indifference toward their physical health status

explanation: Losing a sense like sight or hearing is a massive life change. It's completely natural for patients to feel sad, grieve their independence, and feel a bit isolated. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T8#GNS311_U3_T8_h6)

question: What is the main idea behind convenience sampling?

options.A: Using a computer program to select names randomly
options.B: Asking participants to refer other qualified friends
options.C: Dividing the population into equal demographic groups
options.D: Choosing participants who are easiest to reach and recruit

explanation: You nailed it! Convenience sampling is all about grabbing whoever is readily available—like the students sitting right next to you in class. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T18#GNS224_U1_T18_h4)

question: What is the purpose of performing a bimanual examination right before an MVA starts?

options.A: To determine the exact size and position of the uterus
options.B: To scrape away loose tissue without needing a canula
options.C: To check if the patient's bladder is completely empty
options.D: To measure the patient's blood pressure and pulse rate

explanation: Knowing whether the uterus is tilted forward or backward helps the clinician guide instruments smoothly and prevents accidental perforation. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T010#GNS226_U5_T010_h5)

question: Why is it important to involve local leaders early in a health intervention?

options.A: Their endorsement helps build community trust and cooperation
options.B: It stops ordinary citizens from asking questions
options.C: They are required by law to pay for all medical equipment
options.D: They must personally diagnose every sick patient

explanation: Local populations listen closely to their leaders, making their backing crucial for high community participation. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h4)

question: What happens inside the eye to cause a cataract?

options.A: The drainage tubes get blocked with cellular debris
options.B: Abnormal blood vessels grow and leak under the retina
options.C: Proteins in the lens clump together and form cloudy spots
options.D: The cornea loses its smooth shape and becomes irregular

explanation: Over time, proteins inside the lens break down and bunch up, turning the normally clear lens milky and cloudy. [learn more](GNS311_U3_T3#GNS311_U3_T3_h5)

question: At what specific location do nerve fibers from the inside of each retina cross to the other side?

options.A: Occipital lobe
options.B: Ciliary body
options.C: Optic disc
options.D: Optic chiasm

explanation: The optic chiasm is the X-shaped structure where partial crossover of visual nerve fibers occurs. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h6)

question: A child is rushed to the ward with severe, complicated malaria. What is the best first step regarding their medications?

options.A: Refuse treatment until the family pays cash for the full prescription
options.B: Wait for hospital accountants to review the family's bank statements
options.C: Send the parents out to buy drugs from a commercial chemist across the street
options.D: Provide necessary emergency anti-malarials immediately under the exemption policy

explanation: Spot on! Severe pediatric emergencies qualify for immediate medication access to save the child's life without delay. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h4)

question: Why can't a nurse just study a huge, broad clinical topic without narrowing it down first?

options.A: It lacks the specific focus needed to collect and analyze relevant data
options.B: Patients will not want to participate in broad studies
options.C: Hospital management will refuse to fund broad topics
options.D: It is illegal to research topics that are too wide

explanation: If a topic is too wide (like 'malaria in Nigeria'), you won't know where to start looking. Narrowing it down helps you focus on exact details you can actually measure. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T8#GNS217_U3_T8_h1)

question: What is spiritual distress in a palliative care setting primarily related to?

options.A: Physical exhaustion caused by lack of sleep
options.B: A lack of proper religious education in childhood
options.C: Disagreements between family members over hospital bills
options.D: Struggles with meaning, purpose, forgiveness, and fear of the unknown

explanation: Spiritual and existential distress focuses on deep questions about life's value, unresolved guilt, and the search for peace near the end of life. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T13#GNS321_U4_T13_h4)

question: A nurse wants to test a new handwashing style on two hospital wards without disrupting how the wards are already set up. What is the best study type?

options.A: Retrospective case-control study
options.B: Cross-sectional survey
options.C: Quasi-experimental study
options.D: Randomized controlled trial

explanation: Correct! When you can't randomly mix up individual patients because of real-world ward setups, a quasi-experimental design saves the day. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h4)

question: When a patient reaches the end of life, what is the main focus of nursing care?

options.A: Restricting family visits to maintain strict silence
options.B: Trying aggressive new surgical procedures to cure them
options.C: Focusing only on lab values and medication charts
options.D: Ensuring a peaceful, pain-free, and dignified transition

explanation: When cure is no longer possible, comfort is everything. End-of-life care is all about peace, dignity, and pain control. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T1#GNS221_U4_T1_h8)

question: What is the main goal of doing an occupational health hazard assessment?

options.A: To identify and evaluate potential health and safety risks
options.B: To discipline workers who fail to wear uniforms
options.C: To check the company's financial profits and losses
options.D: To prescribe medications for non-work illnesses

explanation: The main point of a hazard assessment is to spot dangerous conditions early so we can protect workers before anyone gets hurt. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T5#GNS225_U7_T5_h8)

question: What is the most reliable, go-to test used in labs to check for chlamydia and gonorrhea?

options.A: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay
options.B: Microscopic wet mount preparation
options.C: Nucleic acid amplification testing
options.D: Complete blood cell count analysis

explanation: That's right! Nucleic acid amplification testing (NAAT) is super accurate at spotting the genetic material of these bacteria. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T5#GNS216_U5_T5_h5)

question: A patient with stable COPD comes to the clinic asking about their daily routine. Which type of drug is best for long-term management?

options.A: An oral methylxanthine taken once a week
options.B: A long-acting bronchodilator taken every day
options.C: A short-acting rescue inhaler used every morning
options.D: An intravenous steroid given during clinic visits

explanation: For chronic conditions like COPD, consistency is key! Daily long-acting bronchodilators keep baseline symptoms under control so flare-ups happen less often. [learn more](GNS223_U2_T2#GNS223_U2_T2_h4)

question: Why might a newborn infant have slightly swollen breast tissue shortly after birth?

options.A: Early milk production has begun
options.B: Blockage of the lymphatic vessels
options.C: Maternal hormones crossed the placenta
options.D: A congenital infection of the skin

explanation: High levels of maternal hormones circulate in the baby's blood before birth, causing temporary breast enlargement that soon fades. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h7)

question: Why might a patient have high blood urea levels even when their kidneys are completely healthy?

options.A: Excess sodium intake stops the liver from processing urea
options.B: Low physical activity always increases muscle breakdown
options.C: Dehydration or a high protein meal can raise it
options.D: Lack of red blood cells forces the liver to make more urea

explanation: Exactly! Urea is easily influenced by what you eat and how much water you drink. If a patient is dehydrated, urea becomes more concentrated in the blood even without kidney damage. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T9#GNS123_U2_T9_h2)

question: A mother brings her baby for immunization, but the child has a mild runny nose. What should you do?

options.A: Send the child home until all cold symptoms completely disappear
options.B: Refer the child immediately to the main district hospital
options.C: Give half the normal dose because the immune system is busy
options.D: Proceed with the vaccination as minor illness is not a contraindication

explanation: A little sniffle or low fever shouldn't stop life-saving vaccines! Minor illnesses don't block the immune response. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h3)

question: In sickle cell disease, what causes red blood cells to bend into a crescent or 'sickle' shape?

options.A: Abnormal hemoglobin molecules
options.B: Low white blood cell counts
options.C: Excess dietary iron intake
options.D: Rapid platelet activation

explanation: Spot on! The hemoglobin inside the red blood cells has a slight structural change. When oxygen levels drop, these altered molecules stick together and pull the cell into that famous sickle shape. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T14#GNS311_U2_T14_h2)

question: A patient with diabetes looks shaky, dizzy, and is sweating before lunch. What should the nurse do right away?

options.A: Administer the scheduled dose of daily long-acting insulin
options.B: Send a blood sample to the laboratory for an HbA1c test
options.C: Encourage the patient to sleep until the symptoms pass
options.D: Check blood glucose levels and prepare a fast-acting carbohydrate

explanation: Shakiness and sweating are red flags for low blood sugar (hypoglycemia). Always check the blood glucose first and have a fast sugar source ready! Patient safety comes first. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T3#GNS313_U3_T3_h6)

question: When leaving an isolation room, what is the very first piece of PPE you take off?

options.A: Gloves
options.B: Goggles
options.C: Gown
options.D: Mask

explanation: Your gloves have touched the most germs, so they come off first! Always peel them off carefully before touching anything else. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T15#GNS122_U2_T15_h5)

question: Who do state-level anti-FGM laws mostly target for arrest?

options.A: Traditional cutters who perform the procedure
options.B: Local pharmacists selling basic antibiotics
options.C: Mothers who miss child vaccination appointments
options.D: Traditional birth attendants helping with normal deliveries

explanation: Spot on! State laws specifically target the individuals who physically perform the cutting, as well as those who actively sponsor or demand it. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T7#GNS312_U1_T7_h3)

question: A nurse studies if walking 30 minutes daily lowers blood pressure in adults. What is the dependent variable here?

options.A: Blood pressure level
options.B: The time of day
options.C: The adult participants
options.D: Walking 30 minutes daily

explanation: Great job! The dependent variable is the outcome you are measuring—in this case, the blood pressure responding to the walk. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T1#GNS217_U1_T1_h3)

question: A nurse checks a patient's blood pressure thirty minutes after giving a blood pressure medication to see if it dropped into the normal range. Which phase of the nursing process is this?

options.A: Planning
options.B: Evaluation
options.C: Diagnosis
options.D: Assessment

explanation: Checking the results after an intervention to see if goals were met is the definition of the evaluation phase. [learn more](GNS112_U1_T4#GNS112_U1_T4_h8)

question: During which stage of sleep do you experience vivid dreams and temporary muscle relaxation?

options.A: Stage 3 NREM sleep
options.B: Stage 1 NREM sleep
options.C: Stage 2 NREM sleep
options.D: REM sleep

explanation: REM (Rapid Eye Movement) sleep is when most dreaming happens. Your body temporarily relaxes your muscles so you don't act out your dreams! [learn more](GNS211_U3_T17#GNS211_U3_T17_h4)

question: Which of these is an actual 'system-level' fix to improve patient safety?

options.A: Redesigning electronic medication screens to make high-risk doses harder to select
options.B: Warning all nursing staff to pay closer attention during their shifts
options.C: Posting a memo on the staff bulletin board about being careful
options.D: Suspending the nurse involved in the error for a period of two weeks

explanation: That's a true system fix! Changing how a computer system or tool works makes doing the right thing much easier and mistakes much harder to make. [learn more](GST319_U5_T2#GST319_U5_T2_h6)

question: Which of the following is a modifiable risk factor for coronary artery disease?

options.A: Advanced age
options.B: Cigarette smoking
options.C: Family history
options.D: Biological sex

explanation: Smoking can be stopped or managed, making it a modifiable risk factor, unlike age, gender, and family history which cannot be changed. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T4#GNS213_U1_T4_h3)

question: What do second-order neurons typically do in ascending sensory pathways?

options.A: They secrete neurotransmitters onto sweat glands
options.B: They directly connect skin receptors to motor neurons
options.C: They cross the midline and ascend to the thalamus
options.D: They store long-term sensory memories in the frontal lobe

explanation: You got it! Second-order neurons cross over (decussate) to the opposite side of the spinal cord or brainstem before heading up to the thalamus. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T28#GNS211_U3_T28_h5)

question: Which of the following is an example of print IEC material?

options.A: Illustrated leaflets and posters
options.B: Radio jingles and community songs
options.C: Traditional dance and town criers
options.D: Live theatrical drama skits

explanation: Print materials rely on visual text and graphics, such as leaflets, flyers, and posters, to convey health messages. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T4#GNS124_U5_T4_h3)

question: Which nursing action is strictly forbidden during the initial assessment of a patient bleeding in late pregnancy?

options.A: Checking the maternal blood pressure
options.B: Palpating the abdominal wall gently
options.C: Performing a digital vaginal examination
options.D: Monitoring the fetal heart rate

explanation: Never do a digital vaginal exam when late pregnancy bleeding is unexplained, because it can provoke severe hemorrhage if placenta praevia is present! Safety first! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T017#GNS226_U2_T017_h5)

question: How does MBO change performance evaluations for nurses?

options.A: Annual reviews are completely eliminated from the hospital
options.B: Manager opinions matter more than actual patient outcomes
options.C: Appraisals are judged against pre-agreed goals instead of subjective opinions
options.D: Evaluations are done in secret without the nurse knowing

explanation: MBO makes performance reviews objective because both parties measure success against clear targets they agreed on earlier. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h5)

question: Why are the veins in the lower part of the oesophagus so critical during liver disease?

options.A: They prevent stomach acid from washing backward into the throat.
options.B: They supply the main nerve impulses that trigger swallowing waves.
options.C: They carry all arterial blood returning from the entire stomach.
options.D: They form a direct connection between portal and systemic veins.

explanation: Well done! Because these veins link the liver's portal system to the general body circulation, they can bulge and bleed dangerously when liver scarring blocks blood flow. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T2#GNS121_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why is it so important to counsel patients on what to expect physically before they take abortion medications at home?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of the hospital visit.
options.B: It legally waives the clinic from malpractice claims.
options.C: It prepares them for the expected severe cramps and heavy bleeding at home.
options.D: It prevents heavy bleeding from starting too early.

explanation: Exactly! Knowing what normal cramps and bleeding look like helps patients manage their symptoms calmly at home without unnecessary panic. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T011#GNS226_U5_T011_h3)

question: What development after World War II greatly boosted the progress of nursing research?

options.A: The creation of graduate master's programs in nursing
options.B: The invention of the electronic medical record
options.C: The complete replacement of doctors by nurse practitioners
options.D: The banning of all traditional hospital routines

explanation: Master's programs gave nurses the formal scientific training required to design, fund, and conduct independent research studies. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T3#GNS217_U2_T3_h3)

question: What is the primary role of the nurse within the multidisciplinary palliative care team?

options.A: Making all final medical diagnoses and prescribing drugs alone
options.B: Replacing the family members during visiting hours
options.C: Acting as a central hub of communication and coordinating care
options.D: Handling the financial billing and insurance claims for the hospital

explanation: Nurses spend the most time at the bedside, making them uniquely positioned to coordinate input from all team members. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T15#GNS321_U4_T15_h8)

question: Why do newborn babies routinely get a vitamin K injection shortly after birth?

options.A: To reverse potential clotting factor loss from traumatic delivery
options.B: To stimulate immediate production of white blood cells
options.C: To prevent the development of inherited haemophilia
options.D: To make up for a sterile gut that cannot yet synthesize vitamin K

explanation: Babies are born with clean, sterile tummies that haven't grown the helpful gut bacteria needed to make vitamin K yet. That quick injection protects them from bleeding problems! [learn more](GNS311_U2_T10#GNS311_U2_T10_h4)

question: What is the main job of the ureters in our body?

options.A: Filter waste products out of the blood
options.B: Concentrate electrolytes in the renal pelvis
options.C: Store urine until it is ready for excretion
options.D: Transport urine from the kidneys to the bladder

explanation: You've got this! Think of the ureters as plumbing pipes that carry urine from the kidneys down into the bladder. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T2#GNS121_U2_T2_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a classic warning sign of a growing ovarian tumor?

options.A: Urinary urgency or frequency
options.B: Unexplained weight gain in the upper arms
options.C: Persistent abdominal bloating
options.D: Feeling full very quickly after starting a meal

explanation: Correct! Upper arm weight gain is not linked to ovarian tumors, but bloating, feeling full fast, and rushing to the toilet are classic signs. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T33#GNS216_U5_T33_h4)

question: How do social and environmental factors affect a person's emotional state?

options.A: They completely override all biological influences in the human brain
options.B: They have zero effect once a person reaches adulthood
options.C: Economic stability and community support systems directly shape resilience and stress levels
options.D: They only matter if the person has a diagnosed physical disease

explanation: Our surroundings matter! Things like financial stress, safety, and having a good support system directly impact how much daily stress we carry. [learn more](GNS314_U1_T5#GNS314_U1_T5_h2)

question: What is the big difference between bactericidal and bacteriostatic drugs?

options.A: Bactericidal agents require acidic pH, while bacteriostatic agents need alkaline pH
options.B: Bacteriostatic drugs work only in the lungs, while bactericidal drugs work everywhere
options.C: Bactericidal drugs kill bacteria, whereas bacteriostatic drugs stop their growth
options.D: Bacteriostatic drugs destroy human cells, but bactericidal drugs protect them

explanation: Easy to remember: Bacterici-DAL drugs outright KILL the bacteria, while bacteriostatic drugs just press 'pause' on their growth and let your immune system finish the job! [learn more](GNS223_U2_T4#GNS223_U2_T4_h2)

question: Why must you check a patient's kidney function before a contrast-enhanced CT scan?

options.A: Contrast dye can strain the kidneys and worsen poor function
options.B: Poor kidneys make patients allergic to all drugs instantly
options.C: Contrast dye causes the urinary bladder to shut down
options.D: Kidney problems stop the CT machine from taking clear pictures

explanation: Iodine contrast can be tough on the kidneys, so we always check renal function first to keep our patients safe. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T8#GNS222_U3_T8_h6)

question: What is a key priority for a nurse when conducting a sexual health assessment with an adolescent?

options.A: Scolding the teenager for engaging in risky behaviors
options.B: Focusing solely on physical vitals while ignoring mental health
options.C: Ensuring confidentiality and building a trusting relationship
options.D: Reporting every detail immediately to the school principal

explanation: Teens will only share honest information about their sexual health if they trust the nurse and know their secrets are safe. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h9)

question: Which gland releases prolactin into the blood to make milk?

options.A: Thyroid gland
options.B: Posterior pituitary gland
options.C: Adrenal cortex
options.D: Anterior pituitary gland

explanation: You got it! The anterior pituitary releases prolactin whenever the baby suckles, telling your body to keep making milk. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T18#GNS121_U5_T18_h3)

question: What does an endemic disease mean in a community?

options.A: An outbreak that affects only travellers arriving from overseas
options.B: A rare condition that has been completely eradicated by vaccines
options.C: A disease that is constantly present at a predictable baseline level
options.D: A sudden wave of infections that spreads across multiple countries

explanation: An endemic disease maintains a steady, predictable presence within a specific population rather than appearing as a sudden unexpected wave. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h1)

question: Why do we divide an operating suite into unrestricted, semi-restricted, and restricted zones?

options.A: To progressively lower the risk of microbial contamination closer to the patient
options.B: To ensure that doctors and nurses have separate break rooms
options.C: To make it easier to clean the floors with automated machines
options.D: To prevent patients from wandering into the administrative offices

explanation: You got it! These zoning layers act like security checkpoints, filtering out dust and germs step-by-step before anyone steps near the patient. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T2#GNS123_U5_T2_h6)

question: What is the main goal of infection control when caring for patients right inside their own homes?

options.A: Eliminating all microorganisms from the domestic environment
options.B: Transforming the private home into a sterile hospital room
options.C: Reducing the cost of medical equipment maintenance
options.D: Breaking the chain of infection to protect clients and workers

explanation: Spot on! The big picture in home care is always stopping germs from spreading between you and your patient. You've got this! [learn more](GNS324_U6_T9#GNS324_U6_T9_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT a method of environmental vector control?

options.A: Spraying heavy doses of chemical aerosols inside every home
options.B: Clearing stagnant water pools around residential areas
options.C: Cutting away overgrown bushes near houses
options.D: Improving local waste disposal systems

explanation: Spraying chemicals is 'chemical control,' whereas cleaning up bushes, trash, and water pools is 'environmental control' because you're changing their natural habitat. [learn more](GST114_U6_T1#GST114_U6_T1_h6)

question: A patient tells a nurse they only take 'natural' painkillers bought off the supermarket shelf. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Tell the patient that shop-bought drugs do not count as real medication
options.B: Ignore the information since a prescription was not required
options.C: Document and review the OTC use for potential drug interactions
options.D: Immediately report the patient to the hospital pharmacy board

explanation: Even OTC drugs can interact with prescription treatments, so nurses must document and evaluate all self-administered products. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T1#GNS125_U2_T1_h3)

question: What do we mean by the 'window of implantation' in human reproduction?

options.A: The brief number of days when the uterine lining is receptive to a blastocyst
options.B: The days when the cervix opens to allow sperm to enter the uterus
options.C: The time period when the corpus luteum stops producing estrogen entirely
options.D: The exact hour when the sperm successfully penetrates the secondary oocyte

explanation: Correct! The womb is only ready to accept a tiny blastocyst during a very short, specific span of days each month. Learning this makes clinical practice much easier! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T2#GNS121_U6_T2_h3)

question: How do quality improvement teams use data like fall rates and skin injury reports?

options.A: To hide negative clinical outcomes from state regulatory agencies.
options.B: To track performance trends and guide system-wide safety improvements.
options.C: To find individual nurses to blame whenever an accident happens.
options.D: To determine which residents should be discharged immediately.

explanation: Quality improvement isn't about blaming people—it's about spotting trends so we can make our hospital or facility safer for everyone! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T3#GNS324_U5_T3_h8)

question: What is the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading in home care?

options.A: Proper hand hygiene
options.B: Restricting all visitors permanently
options.C: Wearing sterile gowns all day
options.D: Spraying rooms with strong perfumes

explanation: Good old-fashioned handwashing is your best defense! It removes germs and stops them from passing between you and your patients. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T9#GNS324_U3_T9_h6)

question: As a community health nurse in a rural Nigerian village, what should be your top priority to reduce maternal complications?

options.A: Building multi-story tertiary specialist hospitals in every village
options.B: Training and building referral linkages with local traditional birth attendants
options.C: Closing down all local markets to force women to stay home
options.D: Importing expensive fertility treatments from overseas pharmaceutical companies

explanation: Since many women first consult traditional birth attendants in the village, building a friendly working relationship and training them to spot danger signs early saves precious lives! [learn more](GNS216_U1_T1#GNS216_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is the surgery called when a badly damaged joint is completely replaced with an artificial one?

options.A: Arthroscopy
options.B: Arthrodesis
options.C: Osteotomy
options.D: Arthroplasty

explanation: Spot on! Arthroplasty is the medical term for joint replacement surgery using modern metal and plastic implants. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T13#GNS222_U1_T13_h7)

question: How many total antenatal visits does the World Health Organization recommend for a normal, healthy pregnancy?

options.A: At least eight contacts
options.B: Exactly four visits
options.C: Only one per trimester
options.D: Twelve monthly visits

explanation: Global health guidelines recommend a minimum of eight antenatal visits so moms and babies get optimal monitoring and support throughout the journey. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T006#GNS226_U1_T006_h2)

question: What is the primary purpose of a low protein diet?

options.A: To cure chronic infections in the urinary tract
options.B: To increase the speed of digestion in the stomach
options.C: To help the patient gain rapid muscle mass
options.D: To reduce the workload on organs that process waste

explanation: Limiting protein intake decreases the amount of nitrogen waste products that damaged organs must filter and clear from the bloodstream. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T004#GNS227_U6_T004_h1)

question: Why is it so crucial to ask a patient about their past medical history?

options.A: It reveals chronic conditions that affect current symptoms
options.B: It tells you what the patient eats for breakfast
options.C: It replaces the need to ask about the present illness
options.D: It proves whether the patient takes their medication daily

explanation: Exactly! Knowing past health issues helps you understand how older illnesses might be mixing with or causing today's trouble. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T1#GNS124_U6_T1_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT a challenge facing Youth Friendly Services in Nigeria?

options.A: Inadequate funding and poor infrastructure
options.B: Rigid cultural or religious norms
options.C: Lack of trained personnel
options.D: Adequate funding and excess infrastructure

explanation: Correct! Nigeria actually struggles with poor funding and bad infrastructure—having *excess* funding and infrastructure is definitely not one of our problems! [learn more](GNS312_U3_T17#GNS312_U3_T17_h8)

question: What is the primary feature that helps distinguish fat embolism syndrome from other post-fracture complications?

options.A: High fever and visible pus draining from a wound
options.B: Complete lack of pain at the site of the broken bone
options.C: Respiratory distress combined with a petechial skin rash
options.D: Slow bone healing over a period of several years

explanation: Fat globules traveling to the lungs and skin typically cause breathing difficulties paired with a characteristic pinpoint red rash. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T10#GNS222_U1_T10_h9)

question: A teenager raised by uninvolved parents shows signs of severe withdrawal and depression. What is the most likely reason for this?

options.A: Too many strict rules limiting social freedom
options.B: Excessive praise leading to a fragile ego
options.C: An overprotective home environment preventing independence
options.D: Chronic emotional neglect and detachment from caregivers

explanation: When parents are completely detached, children miss out on basic emotional support, which often leads to feelings of loneliness and withdrawal. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T1#GNS314_U4_T1_h2)

question: Why would a doctor choose an EPS instead of just a regular ECG?

options.A: An EPS can trigger and pinpoint complex arrhythmias from inside the heart
options.B: A regular ECG only works while the patient is asleep
options.C: A regular ECG is completely unsafe for older adults
options.D: An EPS requires no preparation or recovery time for the patient

explanation: A normal ECG is like looking at the house from the outside. An EPS goes inside the rooms to find exactly where the faulty wiring is causing the fast heartbeats! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T10#GNS222_U3_T10_h1)

question: Why do healthcare professionals classify traditional practices like female genital mutilation as public health issues rather than private matters?

options.A: They are strictly required by national constitutions
options.B: They cause widespread physical and psychological harm
options.C: They cost hospitals too much money to treat
options.D: They are exclusively performed inside public clinics

explanation: Any practice that inflicts severe, widespread bodily and mental injury on a population falls squarely under public health concern. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h1)

question: What is the standard measurement of the biparietal diameter (BPD) in a full-term baby?

options.A: 9.5 cm
options.B: 8.0 cm

explanation: The biparietal diameter—the distance from one side of the head to the other—is roughly 9.5 centimeters at full term. You'll see this number all the time on ultrasound scans! [learn more](GNS121_U6_T13#GNS121_U6_T13_h4)

question: Which type of evaluation happens right along the way to give you feedback while you are still learning?

options.A: Formative evaluation
options.B: Diagnostic evaluation
options.C: Summative evaluation
options.D: Placement evaluation

explanation: Formative evaluation is like a practice quiz that helps 'form' or improve your skills while you are still learning. [learn more](GST321_U9_T1#GST321_U9_T1_h3)

question: Which of the following is a well-known risk factor for future violent behavior?

options.A: Consistently achieving a high level of formal education
options.B: Living in a household with little to no financial debt
options.C: Taking an active part in school or community sports
options.D: Experiencing abuse or trauma during childhood

explanation: Spot on! Early childhood trauma and seeing domestic abuse at home are strong warning signs for experiencing or committing violence later in life. [learn more](GNS313_U3_T14#GNS313_U3_T14_h3)

question: Which of these is a key advocacy role for a nurse working in a geriatric home?

options.A: Enforcing strict institutional routines without exception
options.B: Ensuring residents retain their dignity and rights
options.C: Making all financial decisions for the resident
options.D: Replacing family members during social visits

explanation: Nurses stand up for older adults to make sure their personal choices and human rights are always respected. You are their voice! [learn more](GNS324_U5_T13#GNS324_U5_T13_h2)

question: Why do hospitals immediately isolate patients showing respiratory symptoms?

options.A: To speed up the administration of intravenous fluids
options.B: To reduce the cost of diagnostic testing supplies
options.C: To prevent transmission to staff and other patients
options.D: To allow patients to sleep without hospital noise

explanation: Isolating patients right away stops airborne droplets from spreading to other vulnerable people in the clinic. Smart nursing practice! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T12#GNS214_U1_T12_h4)

question: What is a reservoir in the context of the chain of infection?

options.A: The natural environment where a pathogen lives and multiplies
options.B: The specific medical instrument used to sterilize wounds
options.C: The physical barrier used to block airborne droplets
options.D: The medication given to destroy harmful bacteria

explanation: A reservoir acts as a home base for the microorganism, which can be a human, animal, or inanimate object. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h2)

question: A stroke patient has weak muscles and needs a little bit of help to move their arm fully. What exercise is best?

options.A: Active-assistive exercises
options.B: Passive range of motion
options.C: Complete bed rest restriction
options.D: Heavy weightlifting resistance

explanation: Teamwork! The patient does as much as they can, and you help finish the movement. That is active-assistive exercise. [learn more](GNS221_U1_T4#GNS221_U1_T4_h2)

question: Which medication class is most commonly used to reduce severe inflammation inside an arthritic joint?

options.A: Inhaled bronchodilators
options.B: Topical antifungal creams
options.C: Oral loop diuretics
options.D: Corticosteroids

explanation: Corticosteroids are powerful anti-inflammatory drugs frequently injected into joints to calm swelling and pain. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h4)

question: What happens to the pelvic joints to help the baby pass through the birth canal during labor?

options.A: They yield and allow slight widening of the pelvic ring.
options.B: They lock firmly in place to protect the spinal cord.
options.C: They shrink in size to push the baby downward.
options.D: They temporarily fuse into a single solid bone.

explanation: Relaxed pelvic ligaments let the bones shift slightly, creating a bit more space for the baby to move safely through the pelvis. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T8#GNS121_U7_T8_h6)

question: What makes a protein source 'complete' in our diet?

options.A: It requires no digestion in the stomach
options.B: It comes exclusively from plant-based foods
options.C: It has zero saturated fat content
options.D: It contains all nine essential amino acids

explanation: Spot on! Complete proteins deliver every single essential amino acid that our bodies cannot make on their own. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T004#GNS227_U4_T004_h2)

question: Which problem-solving model focuses on looking backward after an error to find underlying system failures?

options.A: Random brainstorming
options.B: Trial and error
options.C: Immediate punishment
options.D: Root cause analysis

explanation: Root cause analysis investigates why an incident happened by looking at underlying workplace or system processes. [learn more](GNS112_U3_T7#GNS112_U3_T7_h4)

question: Why is classifying emergencies especially vital when many patients arrive at once?

options.A: It allows nurses to discharge everyone without a full examination
options.B: It ensures limited resources go to the most critical patients
options.C: It ensures all patients are treated in the exact order of arrival
options.D: It completely stops the need for doctors in the emergency room

explanation: When many people need help at the same time, sorting them makes sure that staff and equipment are not wasted on minor issues before severe ones are handled. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T1#GNS315_U2_T1_h1)

question: What does professional accountability primarily require of a nurse?

options.A: Avoid reporting clinical errors made by colleagues
options.B: Make all financial decisions for the hospital ward
options.C: Supervise every task performed by junior medical doctors
options.D: Answer for their own actions and accept the consequences

explanation: You've got this! Accountability simply means owning your clinical choices, standing by your actions, and accepting the outcomes like a true professional. [learn more](GST321_U1_T16#GST321_U1_T16_h6)

question: Why can beating too fast (severe tachycardia) actually make the heart less efficient?

options.A: It blocks electrical signals from reaching the ventricles
options.B: It causes the heart muscle to immediately stop receiving oxygen
options.C: It permanently damages the vagus nerve
options.D: It leaves too little time for the heart chambers to fill with blood

explanation: Imagine trying to fill a bucket with water while someone keeps shaking and emptying it too quickly! If the heart beats too fast, it doesn't get enough time to fill up before pumping again. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T7#GNS111_U2_T7_h3)

question: What is the primary long-term clinical use for thiazide diuretics?

options.A: Reducing intracranial pressure
options.B: Treating severe pulmonary edema
options.C: Treating chronic hypertension
options.D: Reversing acute kidney failure

explanation: Thiazides provide a steady, mild diuretic and blood vessel relaxing effect, making them standard first-line therapy for high blood pressure. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h4)

question: Why is a rectovaginal fistula often psychologically distressing for a patient?

options.A: It causes continuous involuntary passage of gas and stool vaginally
options.B: It prevents the patient from ever walking again
options.C: It causes severe upper abdominal pain after meals
options.D: It immediately leads to total kidney failure

explanation: The uncontrollable leakage of feces and flatus through the vagina causes significant hygiene challenges and social embarrassment. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T13#GNS216_U5_T13_h1)

question: What can happen if naloxone is pushed too fast into a patient who has been using opioids for a long time?

options.A: A sudden drop in heart rate leading to cardiac arrest
options.B: Immediate kidney failure and permanent anuria
options.C: Permanent paralysis of the skeletal muscles
options.D: Sudden and severe withdrawal symptoms like vomiting and agitation

explanation: While naloxone saves lives, pushing it too fast throws the patient straight into harsh withdrawal. They'll wake up throwing up and very agitated, so we push it carefully! [learn more](GNS125_U2_T10#GNS125_U2_T10_h6)

question: Why is uterine cancer often caught early when it is easier to treat?

options.A: It causes noticeable symptoms early in its development.
options.B: It grows extremely slowly compared to other cancers.
options.C: Pain occurs before any abnormal bleeding starts.
options.D: Routine blood tests screen for it every year.

explanation: You got it! Abnormal bleeding usually shows up early, which alerts patients and doctors to check things out quickly. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T23#GNS216_U5_T23_h1)

question: Why are grab bars installed in bathrooms for individuals with physical disabilities?

options.A: To block water from splashing onto the bathroom floor tiles
options.B: To hold towels and washcloths within easy reach of the bathing area
options.C: To serve as hanging storage for lightweight assistive devices
options.D: To provide stable support during transfers on and off the toilet or in the shower

explanation: Wet bathroom surfaces combined with transfers make grab bars essential safety features for preventing falls. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h5)

question: What is the most important first step when assessing a patient suspected of being in a forced marriage?

options.A: Interviewing the patient privately away from family members
options.B: Asking the accompanying spouse to explain the patient's injuries
options.C: Discharging the patient quickly to avoid confrontation
options.D: Calling the police immediately while the family is still in the room

explanation: Private interviews ensure the patient feels safe to speak the truth without fear of retaliation from accompanying relatives. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T10#GNS312_U1_T10_h4)

question: A nurse is reviewing survey data where patients ranked hospital food from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent). Which measures can be used?

options.A: Only the arithmetic mean
options.B: Only the range and variance
options.C: Median and mode
options.D: Mean and standard deviation

explanation: Since these are ranked choices, we can find the middle position (median) and the most frequent rank (mode). You're doing great! [learn more](GNS217_U4_T4#GNS217_U4_T4_h6)

question: What is a key physical difference between a caput succedaneum and a cephalhematoma?

options.A: Cephalhematoma occurs outside the scalp, while caput is inside the brain
options.B: Cephalhematoma always requires immediate surgery, but caput never does
options.C: Caput succedaneum contains pure blood, while cephalhematoma contains serous fluid
options.D: Caput succedaneum crosses suture lines, but a cephalhematoma does not

explanation: Because cephalhematoma is confined beneath the periosteum, it stops strictly at the bone suture lines, whereas caput swelling crosses them freely. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T16#GNS121_U6_T16_h3)

question: Which blood test is more specific for diagnosing acute pancreatitis?

options.A: Hemoglobin
options.B: Lipase
options.C: Creatinine
options.D: Albumin

explanation: Spot on! Serum lipase is the go-to test because it's much more specific to the pancreas than amylase, and it stays elevated longer during an attack. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T7#GNS222_U2_T7_h5)

question: What is the medical term for a fever?

options.A: Hyperkalemia
options.B: Hypothermia
options.C: Pyrexia
options.D: Hypovolemia

explanation: Pyrexia is the official medical term used to describe an elevated body temperature or fever. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T3#GNS221_U3_T3_h2)

question: Which medication is the go-to choice for treating tapeworms and flukes?

options.A: Paracetamol
options.B: Praziquantel
options.C: Pyrantel pamoate
options.D: Amoxicillin

explanation: Spot on! Praziquantel is our frontline medication for clearing out cestodes (tapeworms) and trematodes (flukes). [learn more](GNS223_U3_T7#GNS223_U3_T7_h5)

question: If a patient taking a thioamide medication reports which symptom, should you suspect a serious blood issue like agranulocytosis?

options.A: Slight tremors in fingers
options.B: Mild nausea after meals
options.C: Fever and sore throat
options.D: Dry skin and constipation

explanation: Always take a new fever and sore throat seriously with these meds; it can be an early warning sign of a dangerously low white blood cell count. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T3#GNS223_U7_T3_h7)

question: A researcher measures both blood pressure and salt intake among market traders on the same day. What type of study feature is this?

options.A: Testing a new blood pressure medication over time
options.B: Measuring exposure and outcome at the same time
options.C: Comparing historical records from ten years ago
options.D: Following patients after a surgical intervention

explanation: Spot on! Gathering info on both the suspected cause (salt) and the health outcome (blood pressure) simultaneously is the hallmark of cross-sectional work. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T10#GNS224_U1_T10_h2)

question: What is eutrophication in plain terms?

options.A: A sudden increase of clean mineral nutrients in underground wells
options.B: The natural warming of river water by industrial thermal plants
options.C: Oxygen depletion in water caused by the decomposition of excess algae
options.D: The direct filtration of heavy metals through sandy soil layers

explanation: You got it! Too many nutrients cause massive algae blooms; when those plants die and rot, they suck all the oxygen out of the water. [learn more](GST114_U6_T6#GST114_U6_T6_h5)

question: Why might a patient experience a sudden dangerous drop in heart rate during suctioning?

options.A: A sudden spike in blood pressure from anxiety
options.B: Too much clean air rushing into the stomach
options.C: Stimulation of the vagus nerve in the airway
options.D: An allergic reaction to the sterile glove powder

explanation: The vagus nerve runs close to the airway and triggers a slowing of the heart rate when irritated by the suction catheter. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of using a bowel diary for a patient with incontinence?

options.A: To test the chemical pH of passing stool
options.B: To track patterns of leakage, food intake, and bowel movements
options.C: To measure the exact length of the large intestine
options.D: To replace the need for a physical examination

explanation: A bowel diary provides concrete daily records of when and why accidents happen, helping nurses and doctors plan targeted interventions. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T8#GNS212_U1_T8_h5)

question: What is your immediate nursing action if you notice an umbilical cord prolapse during labor?

options.A: administering an intramuscular dose of oxytocin to speed up delivery
options.B: elevating the presenting fetal part off the cord with a gloved hand
options.C: encouraging the mother to push with maximum effort during contractions
options.D: preparing the patient for immediate induction using prostaglandins

explanation: You got it! You must instantly relieve pressure off the cord with your hand to keep oxygen flowing to the baby until emergency help arrives. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h7)

question: If a patient catches a really strong (virulent) strain of bacteria, what are they most likely to experience?

options.A: A much longer and milder incubation window
options.B: Zero replication inside the lymphatic system
options.C: Complete immunity without ever showing symptoms
options.D: A shorter incubation period with faster symptom onset

explanation: You got it! Highly virulent bugs cause tissue damage rapidly, meaning symptoms pop up much faster. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T9#GNS313_U1_T9_h3)

question: Why is creating a confidential and non-judgmental environment crucial when discussing sexual health?

options.A: It guarantees that no chronic illness will ever develop
options.B: It encourages patients to share sensitive concerns and seek help early
options.C: It prevents patients from ever asking questions about medications
options.D: It is required by law to prescribe over-the-counter vitamins

explanation: Patients will only confide intimate struggles if they trust their nurse will treat them with respect and absolute privacy. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h8)

question: Which of the following is a direct obstetric complication linked to female genital mutilation?

options.A: Gestational diabetes mellitus
options.B: Obstructed labor and tearing
options.C: Pregnancy-induced hypertension
options.D: Hyperemesis gravidarum severity

explanation: Scar tissue from these practices restricts the birth canal, leading to difficult deliveries and severe tearing. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T18#GNS312_U1_T18_h2)

question: If a patient has severe kidney failure, what adjustment would a nurse expect for a drug that is normally cleared by the kidneys?

options.A: Stopping all fluid intake to prevent the drug from diluting in the blood
options.B: Switching the patient immediately to a heavy lipid-soluble oral syrup
options.C: A reduction in the drug dose or an increased time interval between doses
options.D: Giving a double dose to overcome the buildup of metabolic waste

explanation: When kidneys aren't working at full speed, drugs stick around much longer. Nurses must watch out for this and expect lower doses or spaced-out timing to keep patients safe from toxicity! [learn more](GNS125_U1_T4#GNS125_U1_T4_h5)

question: How does social stigma directly affect patients who need post-abortion care?

options.A: It guarantees faster recovery times inside the emergency ward
options.B: It encourages patients to attend more routine health checkups
options.C: It delays patients from seeking timely and life-saving medical attention
options.D: It improves the emotional rapport between nurses and patients

explanation: Spot on! Fear of being judged or mistreated often forces patients to hide their symptoms, delaying the urgent care they need. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T006#GNS226_U5_T006_h7)

question: Which ethical rule reminds nurses to make sure their actions cause no extra harm to a vulnerable patient?

options.A: Non-maleficence
options.B: Veracity
options.C: Autonomy
options.D: Justice

explanation: Non-maleficence simply means 'do no harm'. As nurses, protecting our patients from extra injury or distress is our core duty. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T025#GNS226_U5_T025_h2)

question: If a research study reports a p-value of 0.02, what does that actually mean for the nurse?

options.A: Ninety-eight percent of the patients experienced no relief
options.B: There is a two percent chance the results happened by random chance
options.C: The sample size used in the research was too small
options.D: The intervention failed to show any measurable effect

explanation: P-values measure probability. A 0.02 p-value means you can be 98% confident your results are the real deal, not just a fluke. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T14#GNS217_U4_T14_h6)

question: What do biological indicators test for when placed inside a sterilizer?

options.A: The total weight of the metal trays loaded into the chamber
options.B: The correct color change of paper tape on instrument packs
options.C: The actual destruction of highly resistant bacterial spores
options.D: The exact temperature of the room surrounding the machine

explanation: Spot on! Biological indicators use real, super-tough live spores to prove that the machine is strong enough to kill the hardest-to-beat germs. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T8#GNS122_U2_T8_h5)

question: A newborn at home is limp, blue, and not breathing well even after being dried. What is your immediate next step?

options.A: Wait patiently for five minutes to see if color returns
options.B: Initiate positive pressure ventilation using a neonatal resuscitation bag
options.C: Administer oral sugar water to the infant
options.D: Wrap the baby tightly and hand it to the grandmother

explanation: When a baby is floppy and not breathing, every second counts. Start bag-valve-mask ventilation right away to help them breathe. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T3#GNS225_U3_T3_h5)

question: What is the incubation period of an infectious disease?

options.A: The period between receiving a vaccine and gaining immunity
options.B: The duration a patient remains infectious after recovery
options.C: The time between pathogen entry and the first symptom
options.D: The exact number of days a patient stays in the hospital

explanation: The incubation period starts when germs enter the body and ends when the very first signs of sickness appear. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T84#GNS214_U1_T84_h1)

question: Besides filtering waste and making urine, what other major job do the kidneys have?

options.A: Producing and releasing vital hormones
options.B: Storing bile for fat digestion
options.C: Manufacturing white blood cells
options.D: Synthesizing digestive enzymes

explanation: The kidneys double as endocrine organs that manufacture and release hormones directly into the blood. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T8#GNS121_U2_T8_h1)

question: Why must we encourage patients to drink plenty of water right after a barium meal?

options.A: To prevent the patient from developing a high fever
options.B: To prevent severe constipation caused by the barium
options.C: To dissolve any leftover barium remaining in the stomach
options.D: To speed up the absorption of the contrast into the blood

explanation: Spot on! Barium soaks up water like a sponge as it moves down, so extra fluids save your patient from a hard, painful time in the toilet. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T14#GNS221_U2_T14_h6)

question: Why do nurses monitor patients for a short while right after giving an injection vaccine?

options.A: To watch for acute hypersensitivity or allergic reactions
options.B: To measure the exact antibody titer level in the blood
options.C: To check if the vaccine successfully created memory T cells
options.D: To ensure the patient's innate barriers remain intact

explanation: Even though vaccines are very safe, keeping an eye on patients right after ensures quick help is right there if an unexpected allergy flares up. [learn more](GST114_U4_T1#GST114_U4_T1_h9)

question: When you gently feel (palpate) a mother's tummy to check her uterus after birth, what is your main goal?

options.A: To confirm that the uterus is firm and contracting
options.B: To check if the bladder is completely empty
options.C: To stimulate milk production in the breasts
options.D: To measure the exact weight of the mother

explanation: A nice, hard, contracted uterus (like a firm mango!) stops bleeding. If it feels soft or boggy, that's a red flag for postpartum hemorrhage. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T52#GNS214_U1_T52_h4)

question: Which type of meningitis is a true medical emergency that requires quick action?

options.A: Bacterial meningitis
options.B: Viral meningitis
options.C: Fungal meningitis
options.D: Aseptic meningitis

explanation: Bacterial meningitis moves dangerously fast. Without immediate antibiotics, it can cause severe brain damage or worse. Spotting it early saves lives! [learn more](GNS222_U3_T17#GNS222_U3_T17_h2)

question: A patient arrives at the emergency ward with sudden, sharp one-sided pelvic pain, nausea, and vomiting. What should the nurse suspect first?

options.A: Normal ovulation
options.B: Ovarian torsion
options.C: Simple follicular cyst
options.D: Chronic pelvic pain

explanation: When pain comes on suddenly and sharply on one side with nausea, always keep ovarian torsion on your radar as a surgical emergency! [learn more](GNS216_U5_T32#GNS216_U5_T32_h6)

question: If a hospital ward wants the most accurate count of surgical infections, which method should they use?

options.A: Patient self-reporting through comment cards left in the waiting room
options.B: Annual surveys sent out to former patients via postal mail six months later
options.C: Passive surveillance by waiting for surgeons to submit written feedback forms
options.D: Active surveillance by reviewing lab results and patient charts directly

explanation: Well done! Proactively checking charts and lab results catches infections that busy doctors and nurses might miss through normal reporting. [learn more](GST114_U2_T22#GST114_U2_T22_h3)

question: Which specialized skin cells make the pigment melanin?

options.A: Melanocytes
options.B: Fibroblasts
options.C: Langerhans cells
options.D: Keratinocytes

explanation: Correct! Melanocytes are the clever cells in our lower epidermis that produce melanin. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h5)

question: What historic international conference officially launched the global primary health care movement in 1978?

options.A: The Abuja Health Summit
options.B: The Geneva Nursing Accord
options.C: The Lagos Charter on Health
options.D: The Alma-Ata Declaration

explanation: The Alma-Ata Declaration in 1978 set the foundation for global primary health care and the goal of Health for All. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h1)

question: Which of the following is a major barrier to safe motherhood in Nigeria?

options.A: An overabundance of fully equipped emergency hospitals
options.B: Too many skilled midwives working in remote villages
options.C: Free transportation services for all pregnant women
options.D: Inadequate health infrastructure and out-of-pocket spending

explanation: Poor facilities and the burden of paying out-of-pocket for treatment prevent many Nigerian women from getting timely care. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T44#GNS214_U1_T44_h8)

question: What makes ratio data special compared to other levels of measurement?

options.A: Ratio data lacks any mathematical ordering
options.B: Ratio data can only be used for categorical groups
options.C: Ratio data has uneven spacing between values
options.D: Ratio data has a true, absolute zero point

explanation: You've got this! Ratio levels feature a true zero where zero means none of the item exists at all—like having zero milliliters of urine output. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T1#GNS224_U2_T1_h3)

question: What does Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) measure?

options.A: The minimum calories needed to sustain basic life functions at rest
options.B: The total number of calories burned during heavy physical exercise
options.C: The maximum amount of fat a person can store in adipose tissue
options.D: The exact speed at which the stomach digests dietary protein

explanation: BMR is the baseline energy your body burns just to keep you alive and breathing while you are completely at rest—like keeping the engine idling in neutral. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T8#GNS121_U1_T8_h6)

question: How does setting small, realistic goals during follow-up visits help the patient?

options.A: It ensures the nurse does not have to do any paperwork
options.B: It replaces the need for any professional medical treatment
options.C: It builds their confidence and encourages active participation in recovery
options.D: It guarantees that the patient will never feel stressed again

explanation: Achievable goals empower patients, making them feel capable and involved in managing their own health. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T5#GNS314_U4_T5_h2)

question: How does a fungal skin infection get that classic ring shape?

options.A: Blood vessels constrict in a circular pattern around the pathogen
options.B: The body pushes all bacteria outward toward the skin edge
options.C: Tight clothing creates circular friction marks on the epidermis
options.D: The fungus grows outward from a center point while healing in the middle

explanation: Think of it like ripples in a pond: the fungus spreads outward in a circle to feed, leaving a clearer, healing center behind. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T97#GNS214_U1_T97_h4)

question: What does microbial isolation mean in the lab?

options.A: Killing all living bacteria on a contaminated surface
options.B: Measuring the total weight of soil bacteria
options.C: Separating a single microbe from a mixed population
options.D: Staining microbes to see them under a light microscope

explanation: Great job! Isolation simply means separating one specific type of microorganism from a group so you can study it all by itself. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h1)

question: Why are anti-diarrhea drugs often a bad idea in bacterial food poisoning?

options.A: They can trap harmful pathogens and toxins inside the digestive tract
options.B: They immediately cause severe high blood pressure
options.C: They permanently destroy the kidneys within a few hours
options.D: They stop all absorption of normal daily vitamins

explanation: Stopping your bowels from moving might sound nice, but it actually keeps the dangerous bacteria and their poisons locked inside your body longer! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h6)

question: What is the main difference between clinical fear and general worry?

options.A: It cannot be managed by nursing interventions.
options.B: It is a response to an immediate, identifiable threat.
options.C: It is completely unrelated to physical safety.
options.D: It only occurs after a surgical operation is finished.

explanation: Spot on! Fear pops up when there is a specific, right-in-front-of-you danger, whereas worry tends to be a bit more vague and unfocused. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T11#GNS123_U3_T11_h1)

question: What does 'informed consent' require before you start any clinical procedure on a patient?

options.A: Verbal approval given only by the hospital director
options.B: Signing a document without reading the risks
options.C: Voluntary permission after understanding risks and benefits
options.D: Payment of all hospital bills in advance

explanation: Informed consent is all about respect! The patient must fully understand the treatment, risks, and options, and then freely agree to go ahead. [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h7)

question: When should respiratory hygiene measures start for a patient visiting the hospital?

options.A: At the very first point of entry into the facility
options.B: Only when the patient requests a protective face mask
options.C: After the patient is admitted to an inpatient ward
options.D: Only after a doctor confirms a respiratory diagnosis

explanation: That's right! Catching coughs and handing out masks right at the reception or triage desk stops airborne bugs from spreading in a crowded waiting room. [learn more](GST114_U2_T21#GST114_U2_T21_h5)

question: What is the main difference between a descriptive and an analytical epidemiological study?

options.A: Analytical studies test hypotheses about causes, while descriptive studies only organize basic health data
options.B: Analytical studies are only conducted in hospitals, while descriptive studies happen outdoors
options.C: Descriptive studies require laboratory tests, while analytical studies only use interviews
options.D: Descriptive studies cost more money to run than analytical studies

explanation: You got it! Descriptive research tells us the 'what, where, and when', while analytical research digs deeper to find the 'why'. Keep going! [learn more](GNS214_U1_T77#GNS214_U1_T77_h4)

question: Why do we apply a cold pack to a mum's perineum during the first 24 hours after a vaginal delivery?

options.A: To speed up uterine involution
options.B: To stimulate lochia production
options.C: To reduce swelling and numb pain
options.D: To prevent milk engorgement

explanation: You nailed it! Cold packs narrow the local blood vessels, which keeps swelling down and gives the sore perineal area a nice numbing relief. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T013#GNS226_U3_T013_h7)

question: What is a key feature of algorithmic standing orders?

options.A: They apply only to surgical procedures performed in tertiary hospitals
options.B: They require the nurse to call a doctor before every single step
options.C: They contain blank spaces for the nurse to write their own drug dosages
options.D: They use decision trees with branching questions to guide clinical choices

explanation: Algorithmic standing orders guide the clinician through a series of sequential questions based on patient findings to arrive at the correct care plan. [learn more](GNS124_U6_T6#GNS124_U6_T6_h3)

question: Which factor is most essential for MBO to succeed?

options.A: Strict orders from the chief medical director
options.B: Active participation from staff members
options.C: Frequent changes to nursing uniforms
options.D: Zero budget spending on training

explanation: Staff involvement is vital because people are more committed to goals they help design. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h2)

question: You keep checking your phone while a patient is trying to tell you about their pain. What message does this send?

options.A: Using excessive medical jargon during the assessment
options.B: Failing to establish the correct termination phase
options.C: Stereotyping the patient's cultural background
options.D: Showing impatience and making the patient feel like a burden

explanation: Rushing or splitting your attention makes the patient feel ignored and destroys trust. Always give them your full presence! [learn more](GNS112_U3_T1#GNS112_U3_T1_h5)

question: Why should a nurse ask about a patient's cultural background during a dietary assessment?

options.A: Food choices are deeply tied to beliefs and traditions
options.B: Cultural habits prevent patients from ever developing deficiencies
options.C: Dietary guidelines are identical for every human population
options.D: Hospital kitchens only prepare culturally neutral foods

explanation: Great thinking! Knowing a patient's food culture helps you suggest meals that they will actually enjoy and stick to. [learn more](GNS227_U5_T006#GNS227_U5_T006_h1)

question: Why are finger foods so helpful for patients with advanced dementia during meals?

options.A: It prevents the patient from spilling liquids on their hospital gown
options.B: It guarantees the patient will eat three full meals every single day
options.C: It promotes independence and makes eating easier for confused patients
options.D: It eliminates the need for any nursing staff supervision

explanation: Spot on! When handling cutlery gets confusing, finger foods let patients feed themselves and hold onto their dignity. [learn more](GNS212_U1_T3#GNS212_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the difference between odynophagia and dysphagia?

options.A: Odynophagia involves pain during swallowing, while dysphagia involves difficulty moving food safely.
options.B: Odynophagia only affects liquids, while dysphagia only affects solid foods.
options.C: Odynophagia occurs in the stomach, while dysphagia occurs in the mouth.
options.D: Odynophagia is a mental refusal to eat, while dysphagia is a physical blockage.

explanation: Think of 'odyno-' as painful, so odynophagia means swallowing hurts. Dysphagia means trouble with the mechanics of swallowing. Both make eating tough! [learn more](GNS324_U6_T1#GNS324_U6_T1_h2)

question: How should a nurse document an adverse event in a patient's clinical chart?

options.A: Writing the details only on a personal notebook kept at home
options.B: Including personal opinions on who caused the error
options.C: Using objective, factual observations without assigning personal blame
options.D: Omitting the event entirely to protect the hospital's reputation

explanation: You got it! Clinical notes must stick purely to the facts—describing what happened and the actions taken—without finger-pointing or personal opinions. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T6#GNS312_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is a very common emotional reaction for a nurse who is caught up in the second victim phenomenon?

options.A: Immediate anger directed exclusively at the hospital management
options.B: Complete emotional numbness with zero memory of the event
options.C: Intense guilt and self-doubt regarding clinical skills
options.D: A sense of relief that the error was finally discovered

explanation: It's heartbreakingly common to question your abilities after a mistake. Remember, making an error doesn't mean you're a bad nurse—it makes you human. Be kind to yourself! [learn more](GST319_U6_T4#GST319_U6_T4_h1)

question: Why is self-care considered an absolute must for mental health nurses, rather than just a nice bonus?

options.A: Unmanaged burnout and fatigue can impair clinical judgment and compromise patient safety
options.B: Hospital management requires nurses to log relaxation hours for promotion
options.C: Patients refuse care from nurses who look tired
options.D: It is the only way to avoid ever working night shifts

explanation: You cannot pour from an empty cup! Looking after your own mental health keeps your clinical judgment sharp so you can keep your patients safe. [learn more](GNS314_U6_T4#GNS314_U6_T4_h7)

question: Why is a patient hyperoxygenated right before undergoing tracheobronchial suctioning?

options.A: To force thick mucus plugs to dissolve and loosen up inside the lungs
options.B: To build up an oxygen reserve and prevent dangerous drops during the procedure
options.C: To test if the oxygen tank and flowmeter are working properly
options.D: To help the patient fall into a deep sleep so they feel no discomfort

explanation: Because the suction catheter temporarily removes air from the airway, extra oxygen beforehand protects the patient from sudden hypoxia. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T12#GNS212_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is the common medical term for what we usually call food poisoning?

options.A: Bowel obstruction
options.B: Systemic sepsis
options.C: Foodborne illness
options.D: Gastric influenza

explanation: Foodborne illness is the standard clinical term for sickness caused by eating contaminated food or drink. Great job getting started! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h1)

question: Why shouldn't patients cover skin creams with airtight plastic wraps unless a doctor tells them to?

options.A: It prevents the cream from ever touching the skin surface
options.B: It can trap excessive moisture and increase drug absorption dangerously
options.C: It stops the patient from feeling any local pain relief
options.D: It causes the skin to become permanently discolored

explanation: Airtight wraps act like an oven, trapping heat and moisture, which forces too much medicine into the body all at once. Spot on! [learn more](GNS122_U1_T9#GNS122_U1_T9_h7)

question: At what angle do you insert the needle for an intramuscular (IM) injection?

options.A: 45 degrees
options.B: 90 degrees
options.C: 15 degrees
options.D: 180 degrees

explanation: Straight down! A 90-degree angle ensures the needle punches right through the skin into the deep muscle tissue. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T72#GNS214_U1_T72_h4)

question: A postpartum patient is bleeding heavily and showing signs of shock. What is the most urgent vascular access step?

options.A: Insert two large-bore intravenous cannulas for rapid fluid replacement
options.B: Administer oral rehydration salts slowly through a nasogastric tube
options.C: Set up a single fine-needle peripheral line for routine daily hydration
options.D: Collect a midstream urine sample to check for urinary tract infection

explanation: In an emergency, large-bore IV lines let you pump in fluids and blood fast enough to rescue her blood pressure and beat shock. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T009#GNS226_U3_T009_h5)

question: Which of these is a great example of a drug working without using a receptor?

options.A: An insulin molecule attaching to a muscle cell
options.B: An opioid binding to a brain pain receptor
options.C: A beta-blocker slowing down the heart rate
options.D: An osmotic laxative pulling water into the bowel

explanation: Spot on! Osmotic laxatives rely on physical water movement rather than locking onto cellular receptors to do their job. [learn more](GNS125_U5_T5#GNS125_U5_T5_h4)
