question: Why are young children at a much higher risk of severe scald burns than adults?

options.A: Their bodies contain less water to help absorb heat energy
options.B: They spend more time working directly inside commercial kitchens
options.C: Their skin is thinner and burns much faster at lower temperatures
options.D: They have faster reflexes that cause them to grab hot pans

explanation: Spot on! Children have thinner skin, meaning hot water causes deeper and much faster damage than it would on an adult. [learn more](GNS324_U6_T6#GNS324_U6_T6_h5)

question: Why must high-risk heart patients take antibiotics before certain dental procedures?

options.A: Dental manipulation can introduce bacteria into the bloodstream, which may latch onto damaged heart valves.
options.B: Dental medications frequently interact negatively with cardiac drugs like digoxin.
options.C: Tooth decay directly causes inflammation of the outer pericardial sac.
options.D: Local anesthetics used by dentists weaken the heart muscle permanently.

explanation: Gum bleeding during dental work lets mouth bacteria sneak into the bloodstream. For a vulnerable heart, prophylactic antibiotics act like a shield! [learn more](GNS213_U1_T6#GNS213_U1_T6_h7)

question: What is the very first step in newborn resuscitation if a baby doesn't cry or breathe right after birth?

options.A: Dry thoroughly with warm towels and provide stimulation
options.B: Administer emergency intravenous drugs through the umbilical cord
options.C: Submerge the baby briefly in warm water to shock the system
options.D: Give chest compressions at a rate of 120 beats per minute

explanation: Drying and rubbing the baby warms them up and gives just enough stimulation to get them breathing on their own. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h7)

question: A patient on chemotherapy calls the clinic saying their temperature is 38.5°C. What should you tell them to do?

options.A: Drink plenty of cold fluids and monitor the temperature for another day.
options.B: Apply a cool damp cloth to the forehead to bring down the fever.
options.C: Take a dose of paracetamol and rest in bed until tomorrow morning.
options.D: Come to the hospital immediately for a medical evaluation and blood work.

explanation: Fever in a chemo patient is an emergency because their immune system is low. Quick action can save a life! [learn more](GNS324_U4_T15#GNS324_U4_T15_h7)

question: How do hormone-producing cells in the Diffuse Neuroendocrine System (DNES) differ from traditional glands?

options.A: They consist exclusively of modified postganglionic sympathetic neurons derived from neural crest tissue
options.B: They possess specialized ducts that empty their chemical secretions directly into the lumen of the gastrointestinal tract
options.C: They lack a blood supply entirely and rely purely on local nervous system stimulation for hormone distribution
options.D: Their hormone-producing cells are scattered singly among other mucosal cell types rather than clustered in a dedicated gland

explanation: Instead of sitting together in one organ (like the thyroid), DNES cells are scattered solo across places like your gut lining, quietly sending out local chemical signals. [learn more](GNS211_U1_T2#GNS211_U1_T2_h7)

question: How do non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) mainly work in the body?

options.A: By putting the central nervous system to sleep
options.B: By releasing natural endorphins in the spine
options.C: By attaching straight to brain opioid receptors
options.D: By blocking prostaglandins at the injury site

explanation: NSAIDs like ibuprofen stop the body from making prostaglandins—the chemical helpers that cause swelling and pain right where you got hurt. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T2#GNS123_U3_T2_h5)

question: A nurse is checking a 15-year-old girl who feels very tired, dizzy, and has pale nail beds. What is the best first step to take?

options.A: Test her for color blindness
options.B: Order an immediate full-body MRI scan
options.C: Do a mandatory neurological reflex exam
options.D: Check her BMI growth chart and ask what she usually eats

explanation: You got it! Growth charts and a simple diet history help nurses quickly spot physical growth patterns and nutritional gaps causing that fatigue. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T010#GNS227_U2_T010_h7)

question: Why do nurses do a cultural assessment for patients?

options.A: To satisfy mandatory hospital paperwork requirements only
options.B: To convince the patient to adopt Western medical practices
options.C: To understand the patient's beliefs and values in order to provide individualized care
options.D: To determine the financial income of the patient's household

explanation: Wonderful! Cultural assessments help us respect our patients' traditions and beliefs, making sure our care fits their unique lifestyle. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T1#GNS123_U2_T1_h5)

question: What is the main goal of birth preparedness and complication readiness (BPCR) during antenatal care?

options.A: To train family members to deliver the baby at home safely
options.B: To prevent dangerous delays in reaching emergency obstetric care
options.C: To remove the financial cost of hospital supplies completely
options.D: To guarantee that the baby is born on the exact estimated date

explanation: BPCR is all about planning ahead (transport, funds, blood donors) so that if an emergency strikes, the mother doesn't lose precious time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T49#GNS214_U1_T49_h6)

question: Think of a research design as a step-by-step plan. What is its main job in nursing?

options.A: To secure ethical approval from the hospital board
options.B: To calculate the exact financial cost of a hospital study
options.C: To write the final reference list for a journal article
options.D: To act as a blueprint for answering a clinical question

explanation: Spot on! Just like building a house needs a good plan, a research design is your overall framework that guides how you answer a specific clinical question. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T3#GNS224_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is it so important to set clear, specific objectives during the planning stage?

options.A: It guides what activities to do and helps measure future success
options.B: It replaces the need to collect baseline data
options.C: It guarantees that no unexpected problems will ever occur
options.D: It ensures that nurses never have to work in rural areas

explanation: Clear objectives act like a map. They show you your daily steps and let you check later whether you actually reached your destination. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T2#GNS124_U3_T2_h7)

question: What is the primary reason for initiating a patient referral to another facility?

options.A: The hospital building needs routine plumbing repairs
options.B: The patient's clinical needs exceed current facility resources
options.C: The attending doctor wants to take a short vacation
options.D: The patient complains about the food quality on the ward

explanation: Referrals are done when specialized care, advanced equipment, or specific expertise is required that the current health center cannot provide. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T5#GNS112_U2_T5_h4)

question: A junior nurse sees a mother bleeding heavily after birth but stays quiet because she is scared of the senior doctor. What kind of barrier is this?

options.A: Hierarchical barrier
options.B: Equipment failure
options.C: Alert fatigue
options.D: Confirmation bias

explanation: Spot on. Strict hospital ranks can make junior staff too intimidated to speak up. Patient safety means every voice matters, no matter your rank! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T7#GNS312_U5_T7_h4)

question: How does climate change directly throw a wrench into farming and crop production?

options.A: Through erratic rainfall, droughts, and rising temperatures
options.B: By making all soils permanently rich and fertile
options.C: Through the complete elimination of all plant pests
options.D: By lowering the global demand for food

explanation: Unpredictable weather, sudden dry spells, and scorching heat mess up traditional planting seasons and ruin harvests. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T024#GNS227_U2_T024_h7)

question: Where do home health care services primarily take place?

options.A: A specialized outpatient clinic
options.B: A long-term nursing facility
options.C: An acute care hospital ward
options.D: The client's personal residence

explanation: Spot on! Home health care brings professional nursing straight to where the client lives. It's all about comfort and care right at home. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T3#GNS324_U1_T3_h1)

question: In the emergency stabilization framework used before transport, what does the letter 'B' stand for?

options.A: Bandaging
options.B: Brain
options.C: Bleeding
options.D: Breathing

explanation: Think of the trusty ABCDE framework! 'B' stands for Breathing, making sure air is moving properly into the lungs right after checking the airway. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T8#GNS315_U3_T8_h3)

question: What is the main benefit of encouraging nurses to report 'near misses' in the clinic?

options.A: It allows managers to calculate exact salary deductions for staff
options.B: It gives the hospital legal protection against malpractice lawsuits
options.C: It fulfills mandatory federal tax reporting requirements
options.D: It helps the unit fix system flaws before a real patient injury happens

explanation: Near misses act like early warning signs, giving the team a chance to fix hidden dangers before a patient gets hurt. [learn more](GST321_U1_T19#GST321_U1_T19_h7)

question: A patient with gallbladder trouble feels pain up near their right shoulder blade. What is this called?

options.A: Referred pain
options.B: Phantom pain
options.C: Rebound tenderness
options.D: Somatic pain

explanation: Referred pain happens when internal organs and skin areas share the same spinal cord pathways, tricking the brain into feeling the pain somewhere else. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T11#GNS213_U3_T11_h3)

question: What is a major lung complication that often happens to patients who are unconscious and immobile for a long time?

options.A: Hypostatic pneumonia
options.B: Pulmonary hypertension
options.C: Asthma exacerbation
options.D: Spontaneous pneumothorax

explanation: Keep learning! When patients stay still, fluids pool at the back of their lungs, making it easy for bacteria to grow and cause pneumonia. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T5#GNS221_U3_T5_h6)

question: What happens when a patient with a weak pancreas eats a heavy, fatty meal?

options.A: All excess fat is stored safely in the liver.
options.B: Unabsorbed fats pass through, causing oily stools and cramping.
options.C: The stomach completely stops all digestion permanently.
options.D: Fats instantly convert into muscle tissue.

explanation: Without enough pancreatic enzymes to break it down, fat passes right through the gut, leading to uncomfortable cramps and oily stools (steatorrhea). [learn more](GNS227_U6_T005#GNS227_U6_T005_h2)

question: Which of the following is a major risk factor for respiratory complications in the ICU?

options.A: Eating a high-protein hospital diet
options.B: Mechanical ventilation and artificial airways
options.C: Having normal blood pressure readings
options.D: Walking in the hallway twice a day

explanation: Artificial airways and mechanical ventilators bypass normal body defenses, making it much easier for bacteria to cause pneumonia and for lung tissue to collapse. [learn more](GNS321_U2_T4#GNS321_U2_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT part of an active drug history?

options.A: Past allergies or reactions to the substance
options.B: The dose and how often the drug is taken
options.C: The patient's childhood immunization record
options.D: The exact brand or generic name of the drug

explanation: Immunizations are part of the general medical history, not an active daily drug history. Every question you answer makes clinical practice clearer! [learn more](GNS215_U2_T2#GNS215_U2_T2_h3)

question: A 10-day-old baby has mild eyelid swelling and watery discharge. Which germ is most likely the cause?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Silver nitrate drops
options.C: Escherichia coli
options.D: Chlamydia trachomatis

explanation: Spot on! Chlamydia tends to show up a bit later than gonorrhea—usually between 5 and 14 days after birth. You're building solid clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T019#GNS226_U3_T019_h3)

question: How do poor internet and lack of journal access affect local nursing research?

options.A: They prevent nurses from wearing their uniforms to work
options.B: They force patients to travel abroad for medical treatments
options.C: They increase the number of medication errors in the wards
options.D: They make thorough literature reviews and data analysis very difficult

explanation: Spot on. Without good internet access, checking what other researchers around the world have discovered becomes a massive struggle. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T6#GNS217_U2_T6_h3)

question: Why do dietitians need to understand human behavior along with food science?

options.A: Food chemistry changes completely based on the patient's mood
options.B: Patients need to feel understood in their cultural and personal habits to follow meal plans
options.C: Biochemical data alone is enough to change eating habits permanently
options.D: Psychological evaluations are legally required before writing a hospital diet

explanation: Knowing the science of food is only half the battle! If a patient's personal or cultural beliefs clash with the diet, they won't be able to follow it. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T001#GNS227_U4_T001_h1)

question: A patient has been on strict bed rest for several weeks. What is likely happening to their bones?

options.A: Calcium storage in the bones is doubling
options.B: Bone-building cells are rapidly making the bones thicker
options.C: Bone breakdown (resorption) is happening faster than bone building
options.D: Spongy bone is turning into solid metal-like columns

question: A patient pulled from a smoky room is restless, confused, and breathing fast. What do these signs tell you first?

question: What happens to a reflex if the sensory neuron gets damaged or cut?

question: Why is teamwork across different sectors necessary when addressing the health needs of unemployed persons?

question: Why must a nurse leader look at all four parts of Deming's framework together?

options.C: Because the four components overlap and deeply influence one another in real practice

question: What is the main job of the mucosa, the innermost layer of your gut?

question: Which type of transmission involves bugs like mosquitoes or ticks passing on an infection?

question: What emergency procedure is used to drain extra fluid from around the heart during cardiac tamponade?

question: Who authored the famous medieval medical text *The Canon of Medicine*?

question: As a nurse, why should you keep a close eye on a patient for a short while right after giving a vaccine?

options.A: To watch for acute allergic reactions or anaphylaxis

question: What is the best reason to use open-ended questions when talking with a PAC patient?

options.A: They shorten the overall time required for the nursing interview
options.B: They prevent the client from crying during the conversation
options.C: They legally protect the hospital from malpractice lawsuits

question: If a head nurse delegates a procedure to a junior colleague, who still holds the ultimate accountability?

options.A: The head nurse who delegated the task

options.D: The junior staff member who performed the task

question: A nurse notices a husband is dominating the conversation and suspects his wife is hiding health issues. What is the best first step?

question: Which type of sensory receptors inside the ear pick up sound and movement?

question: Which heart chamber pumps deoxygenated blood into the pulmonary trunk?

question: What happens if someone's visual association area is damaged, but their primary visual cortex is completely fine?

question: What is the primary purpose of establishing a referral pathway for home delivery?

question: A patient on a new BP medication feels dizzy when standing up. What should you do first as the nurse?

question: Why do midwives often prefer a continuous running stitch instead of separate knots for a second-degree tear?

question: Why does the body need to control hormone release very carefully?

question: For a first-time mother in active labour, how fast should the cervix open?

question: Which part of the brain releases Gonadotropin-Releasing Hormone (GnRH) to kick off the hormone feedback loop?

question: What is the primary focus of critical care nursing?

question: Which type of abuse involves controlling money and financial resources to keep power over a partner?

question: Which changes in the body help trigger the refractory period?

question: What must the urinary sphincters do so that normal urination can happen?

question: What does the maternal mortality ratio actually measure?

question: A nurse is preparing to feed a patient via a PEG tube. What action should be performed first?

question: What is the biggest danger after a quality improvement project hits its initial goals?

question: What is the main goal of doing a 'medication reconciliation' when a patient is admitted?

question: What is the primary purpose of using the topical route of administration?

options.A: To guarantee immediate intravenous bloodstream entry
options.B: To force rapid first-pass liver metabolism of the drug
options.C: To treat a local condition directly on a body surface
options.D: To bypass the need for any skin or mucous membrane contact

explanation: Topical medications are primarily applied directly to the skin or mucous membranes to treat surface-level issues right where they are placed. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T16#GNS125_U3_T16_h1)

question: For which patient condition is elective laparoscopy usually unsafe?

options.A: Stable asymptomatic gallstones
options.B: Mild controlled essential hypertension
options.C: A history of a single childhood hernia
options.D: Severe uncorrected bleeding disorders

explanation: Correct! If a patient has a severe bleeding problem that hasn't been fixed, putting in surgical instruments can cause dangerous internal bleeding. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T5#GNS221_U2_T5_h3)

question: What causes moral distress for a primary health care nurse?

options.A: Having too many administrative meetings with government officials
options.B: Receiving regular feedback from satisfied community members
options.C: Knowing the correct patient care needed but lacking the resources to deliver it
options.D: Working standard daytime hours in a rural health post

explanation: Moral distress happens when a nurse knows the right clinical action to take but systemic shortages prevent them from doing it. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T7#GNS124_U2_T7_h8)

question: When you look at a standard X-ray, what color do dense structures like bones usually appear?

options.A: Bright green
options.B: Pitch black
options.C: Bright white
options.D: Transparent clear

explanation: Bones block the X-ray beams from passing through to the film, creating a bright white picture. You've got this! [learn more](GNS123_U2_T10#GNS123_U2_T10_h1)

question: Which phrase should the nurse avoid saying to a grieving family member?

options.A: I am so sorry for your loss
options.B: Would you like to talk about him?
options.C: I am here for you if you need me
options.D: Time heals all wounds

explanation: Clichés like 'time heals all wounds' can feel dismissive and minimize the real pain the person is feeling. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T8#GNS321_U4_T8_h6)

question: Why do children have different nutritional needs compared to adults?

options.A: Children require fewer calories per kilogram of body weight
options.B: Children do not need micronutrients until puberty begins
options.C: Adults have higher metabolic demands than growing children
options.D: Children are actively building new tissue and growing rapidly

explanation: Spot on! Growing kids need extra fuel and building blocks because their bones, muscles, and organs are developing fast. You've got this! [learn more](GNS227_U2_T006#GNS227_U2_T006_h1)

question: Where is the scheduled date for a child's next vaccine dose primarily recorded for the mother to see?

options.A: On the pharmacy prescription ledger
options.B: On the child's home-based health card
options.C: In the national budget allocation report
options.D: In the local government tax receipt

explanation: The child health card stays with the caregiver and serves as the primary personal reminder for upcoming immunization dates. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T74#GNS214_U1_T74_h3)

question: How does the VAPP Act change how society and the law view domestic abuse within homes?

options.A: It turns domestic abuse into a punishable criminal offense.
options.B: It leaves punishment to traditional village elders.
options.C: It requires financial compensation without any legal trial.
options.D: It treats domestic abuse as a private family dispute.

explanation: Well done! Domestic abuse is no longer seen as a mere 'family secret' or private affair—it is a crime with legal consequences. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T14#GNS312_U4_T14_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard emergency maneuver used during shoulder dystocia?

options.A: applying downward pressure above the maternal pubic bone
options.B: flexing the maternal legs sharply up toward her abdomen
options.C: administering strong uterine relaxants intravenously
options.D: summoning immediate pediatric and obstetric assistance

explanation: Spot on! For shoulder dystocia, we use physical repositioning (like the McRoberts maneuver) and suprapubic pressure rather than IV uterine relaxants. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T001#GNS226_U3_T001_h7)

question: Which action using both hands is a leading cause of accidental needle-stick injuries among nurses?

options.A: Wiping skin with alcohol
options.B: Transporting safety boxes
options.C: Opening glass ampoules
options.D: Recapping used needles

explanation: Trying to guide a used needle back into its tiny cap with two hands is a classic hazard. That's why safety rules tell us never to recap used needles! [learn more](GNS122_U4_T5#GNS122_U4_T5_h2)

question: You examine a child in a rural clinic and notice dry eyes and Bitot's spots. What deficiency should you suspect?

options.A: Vitamin C
options.B: Iron
options.C: Vitamin A
options.D: Calcium

explanation: Dry eyes and Bitot's spots are textbook signs of a Vitamin A deficiency. Great clinical catch! [learn more](GNS124_U6_T5#GNS124_U6_T5_h3)

question: Why do most pregnancy skin changes need no medical treatment?

options.A: Maternal skin becomes completely immune to disease
options.B: The placenta blocks all medications from working
options.C: Hormones stop circulating after the first trimester
options.D: They are normal body responses that fade after delivery

explanation: No stress here! Changes like darkening skin are just harmless body responses to pregnancy hormones that naturally get better after birth. [learn more](GNS121_U7_T9#GNS121_U7_T9_h1)

question: At what point should you label a specimen container with the patient details?

options.A: Only after the laboratory technician asks for confirmation
options.B: Immediately at the bedside in the presence of the patient
options.C: After returning to the nursing station at the end of the shift
options.D: Before entering the patient room to save working time

explanation: Always label right at the bedside! Doing it later invites dangerous mix-ups between patients. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T4#GNS112_U6_T4_h7)
